rationale: Source and benchmark evidence rules out config-only, Vite-plugin, partial-loader, compile/remap, and permanent Prettier solutions. A pinned native OXC fork is the least invasive option that can preserve original spans, reuse oxlint/oxfmt engines, satisfy Vite+ binary resolution, support native LSPs, and retain arena-based performance. T003 is deliberately a user-observable native oxlint slice with red-to-green CLI and performance proof; formatter, complete grammar, Vite+, editor, packaging, Markless, and clean-room work remain mandatory.

worker_package.objective: Import and pin OXC source SHA 129b759131ec60294bfcc0f388a45264c8740507, then deliver a native oxlint vertical slice for a provenance-recorded .tsrx fixture containing TypeScript, an @{ function body, JSX, and @if/@else. The project-built CLI must report no-debugger and no-unused-vars at original TSRX locations, apply one proven-safe standard descendant fix such as no-var, reparse the result, preserve ordinary TSX behavior, and pass frozen P01/P02/P03 performance gates. Begin with retained black-box and performance tests that fail against stock OXC.
